Guide

Export a YouTube transcript without timestamps using BYTE

Save available captions as a continuous text block or keep one timestamp per line. A same-video comparison shows both actual BYTE outputs.

By At Hand Tools · 2026-11-21

On this page

  • First, decide whether you need a file
  • Choose the format before downloading
  • What the cleaner file does, and does not, contain
  • Two real exports from the same video
  • Keep a timed reference when you need to check a quote
  • What about a summarizer or a phone?

Want the words without a time marker before every line? With BYTE on desktop Chrome, turn off Timestamps before exporting. Keep Video title and Video URL so the readable copy still points back to its source.

Removing timestamps changes the layout, not the accuracy of the captions. It is not a summary, a translation, or a verbatim transcript certified against the audio.

First, decide whether you need a file

For reading along once, start with YouTube’s built-in transcript. Its current help describes opening Show transcript from the video description and selecting a caption line to jump to that moment.

The timestamp-toggle problem is real, but the interface is not identical for everyone. A March 2026 Reddit discussion describes losing that control after a panel change. That is a user report, not proof that YouTube removed the option for every account or that it remains missing today.

If your own panel offers a timestamp toggle and a simple copy is enough, use it. BYTE is useful when you want a saved caption file without a separate timestamp-cleanup step.

Choose the format before downloading

At Hand Tools makes BYTE. We verified these controls and both downloads in desktop Chrome using BYTE 0.9.2 from the Chrome Web Store.

  1. In desktop Chrome, open a captioned video with BYTE installed.
  2. Open Transcript settings beside the export controls.
  3. Choose Markdown (.md) for a document with headings and source details, or Text (.txt) for a simpler file.
  4. Turn Timestamps off. Under Included details, retain Video title and Video URL; channel information can help distinguish similarly named videos.
  5. Choose the caption language you actually want, close settings, then select Download transcript.
  6. Open the downloaded file. Check the source URL and the text. Verify the language when choosing the caption track; the example files do not state the language in their headers. An export error is not a saved transcript.

Turning timestamps off affects a new export. It cannot remove timing markers from a file you already downloaded. For an earlier file, preserve the original and export another copy rather than applying a broad search-and-replace that might erase numbers in the narration.

What the cleaner file does, and does not, contain

The current formatter joins caption segments with spaces when timestamps are disabled. It does not write an essay, add useful paragraph breaks, or identify speakers. A long video can therefore produce one long body paragraph. Your text editor’s word wrap can make that easier to read without changing the saved text.

The source also strips bracketed caption annotations before formatting. This matters if sounds, music or other non-speech cues are important to your task. Do not describe the export as an exact archival copy of everything in the caption track.

Two real exports from the same video

On November 20, 2026 (UTC), we exported NASA’s #AskNASA: What is Artemis? twice in Markdown with Original language selected. We kept the same included details and changed only Timestamps.

  • Timestamps on: 3,709 bytes and 83 caption lines with time markers, from 0:03 to 2:52.
  • Timestamps off: 2,964 bytes and one continuous body line with no time markers.
  • In both files: the same title and source URL. After ignoring the time markers and line breaks, all 534 caption words matched in order.

The timed file starts with these two markers. Each caption line is shortened here, as shown by the ellipses:

[0:03] hi i'm serena chancellor …
[0:05] astronaut and this is …

The untimed file starts with those same words without the two time markers or the line break. Choose the copy that fits your task: short timed lines for finding a moment, or an untimed body for reading. These are caption excerpts, not quotations checked against the audio.

Keep a timed reference when you need to check a quote

A timestamp-free file can be easier to read continuously, but it loses the direct time markers useful for checking a passage. If you intend to cite the speaker, retain a second timestamped export or return to YouTube’s transcript. Check the original audio and surrounding visual context before quoting.

BYTE exports available captions. It cannot supply missing captions by listening to the audio. YouTube warns that automatic captions can misrepresent speech; removing timestamps does not improve their accuracy. Exporting a file does not grant permission to republish the transcript.

What about a summarizer or a phone?

A clean transcript and an AI summary are different outputs. YouTube Summary & ChatGPT by Glasp displayed 100,000 users on its Store listing checked on 18 November 2026. Its listing advertises transcript copying and AI summaries. We have not tested its current operation; that public user count is not active usage or a reliability score.

BYTE’s workflow here is desktop Chrome, not an Android workaround. An older r/techsupport question specifically asks about the inconvenience of copying and stripping timestamps on a phone. The friction is relevant, but this guide must not claim to solve the phone constraint.

Use the simplest option that produces the output you need: YouTube for one reading session; BYTE for an inspectable saved caption file; a separate summarizer only when you actually want a summary.
